Start worker sessions and get them ready to sample

Source: R/ctBackendWarmWorkers.R
dot-ctBackendWarmWorkers.Rd

Launches `workers` background R sessions and sets each one evaluating one gradient for `object`, which is what forces Julia to build the objective and compile the engine for this model's shape. Returns immediately: the sessions work while the caller carries on.

Usage

.ctBackendWarmWorkers(
  object,
  workers,
  values = NULL,
  threads = 1L,
  layer = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

A prepared `ctJuliaModel` or a `ctJuliaFit`.

workers

How many sessions to start.

values

Parameter vector to evaluate at. Any finite point compiles the same code; a fit's own estimate is the natural choice when there is one.

threads

Julia threads each worker's session starts with, one for all or one per worker (`.ctBackendWorkerThreads()`). Fixed when the session starts, so a pool warmed at other widths is replaced rather than reused.

layer

Whether the work the workers will do evaluates the layer (`.ctJuliaObjective(layer = TRUE)`, SAEM's kernel) rather than the fit's objective, so each builds and compiles the objective its chains use.

Value

A list of future handles, or `NULL` when warming is unavailable.

Details

The sessions persist. `future::multisession` keeps its pool across calls, so the warmed sessions are the same ones a later chain runs in – which is the point, and the reason this sets a plan rather than making a one-shot cluster.
